newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Gabon cited as possible venue for Zaire peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Gabon cited as possible venue for Zaire peace talks.

text.p: Negotiators are considering Gabon as a venue to break deadlock over where to hold a planned meeting between Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, a presidential spokesman said on Friday.
"Gabon has been proposed, but we are waiting for confirmation from all sides," Mobutu's spokesman Professor Kabuya Lumuna told Reuters.

"If we exclude the others that have been rejected, Gabon is perhaps the most likely place now. I know that they (rebels) have sent envoys there," he added. A Zairean newspaper reported on Friday that Kabila's foreign affairs spokesman and leading negotiator, Bizima Karaha, was in Gabon on Thursday.

Earlier this week Mobutu declined an invitation from President Nelson Mandela to meet Kabila in South Africa, saying the long flight was too arduous for a man still convalescing from prostate cancer surgery.
Kabila rejected Mobutu's choice of Congo as an alternative venue and instead proposed the rebel-held city of Lubumbashi.
"Obviously you do not go for such a meeting on enemy territory," Kabuya said, referring to Kabila's latest proposal.
